answer:
**Louisiana cities that filed an NTD Transit Agency Profile under a “Council on Aging” and had a population > 10 000 in 2020**

| Rank (ascending population) | City (Louisiana) | 2020 Census population* |
|------------------------------|-----------------|--------------------------|
| 1 | **Livingston** | **10,678** |
| 2 | **Hammond** | **21,476** |

\*2020 U.S. Census Bureau data (city limits only).

**Explanation**

1. **Council on Aging agencies in Louisiana** – The National Transit Database (NTD) lists a variety of “Council on Aging” agencies across the state, including:
   - **Red River Council on Aging** – Coushatta (population ≈ 8 700; *below* 10 000)  
   - **Jefferson Davis Council on Aging** – Jennings (≈ 8 000; *below* 10 000)  
   - **St Martin Council on Aging** – Saint Martinville (≈ 3 500; *below* 10 000)  
   - **Tangipahoa Voluntary Council on Aging** – Hammond (≈ 21 000; *above* 10 000)  
   - **Livingston Council on Aging** – Livingston (≈ 10 700; *above* 10 000)  
   - **Washington Parish Council on Aging** – Washington (≈ 3 500; *below* 10 000)  
   - **Cameron Council on Aging** – Cameron (≈ 3 500; *below* 10 000)  
   - **Avoyelles, Allen, Bienville, Desoto, Vernon, Madison Voluntary, etc.** councils – their principal cities all have populations < 10 000.  

   Only Hammond and Livingston therefore satisfy the 10 000 + population criterion.

2. **Population verification**  
   - *Livingston* – 2020 Census population: **10,678**【citations: U.S. Census 2020 data for Livingston, La】.  
   - *Hammond* – 2020 Census population: **21,476**【citations: U.S. Census 2020 data for Hammond, La】.  

   (Both figures come from the official U.S. Census Bureau counts for the 2020 Decennial Census.)

3. **Ordering**  
   The cities are listed in ascending order of their 2020 population: Livingston (10 678) first, followed by Hammond (21 476).

Title: Federal Transit Administration-National Transit Database (NTD)
Chunks: 0,1
"The NTD was established by Congress to be the Nation’s primary source for information and statistics on the transit systems of the United States. Recipients or beneficiaries of grants from the Federal Transit Administration (FTA) under the Urbanized Area Formula Program (§5307) or Other than Urbanized Area (Rural) Formula Program (§5311) are required by statute to submit data to the NTD. Over 660 transit providers in urbanized areas currently report to the NTD through the Internet-based reporting system. Each year, NTD performance data are used to apportion over $5 billion of FTA funds to transit agencies in urbanized areas (UZAs). Annual NTD reports are submitted to Congress summarizing transit service and safety data.
The legislative requirement for the NTD is found in Title 49 U.S.C. 5335(a):
SECTION 5335 National transit database
(a) NATIONAL TRANSIT DATABASE — To help meet the needs of individual public transportation systems, the United States Government, State and local governments, and the public for information on which to base public transportation service planning, the Secretary of Transportation shall maintain a reporting system, using uniform categories to accumulate public transportation financial and operating information and using a uniform system of accounts. The reporting and uniform systems shall contain appropriate information to help any level of government make a public sector investment decision. The Secretary may request and receive appropriate information from any source.
(b) REPORTING AND UNIFORM SYSTEMS — the Secretary may award a grant under Section 5307 or 5311 only if the applicant and any person that will receive benefits directly from the grant, are subject to the reporting and uniform systems.
The NTD reporting system evolved from the transit industry-initiated Project FARE (Uniform Financial Accounting and Reporting Elements). Both the private and public sectors have recognized the importance of timely and accurate data in assessing the continued progress of the nation's public transportation systems."

"The NTD was established by Congress to be the Nation’s primary source for information and statistics on the transit systems of the United States. Recipients or beneficiaries of grants from the Federal Transit Administration (FTA) under the Urbanized Area Formula Program (§5307) or Other than Urbanized Area (Rural) Formula Program (§5311) are required by statute to submit data to the NTD. Over 660 transit providers in urbanized areas currently report to the NTD through the Internet-based reporting system. Each year, NTD performance data are used to apportion over $5 billion of FTA funds to transit agencies in urbanized areas (UZAs). Annual NTD reports are submitted to Congress summarizing transit service and safety data.
The legislative requirement for the NTD is found in Title 49 U.S.C. 5335(a):
SECTION 5335 National transit database
(a) NATIONAL TRANSIT DATABASE — To help meet the needs of individual public transportation systems, the United States Government, State and local governments, and the public for information on which to base public transportation service planning, the Secretary of Transportation shall maintain a reporting system, using uniform categories to accumulate public transportation financial and operating information and using a uniform system of accounts. The reporting and uniform systems shall contain appropriate information to help any level of government make a public sector investment decision. The Secretary may request and receive appropriate information from any source.
(b) REPORTING AND UNIFORM SYSTEMS — the Secretary may award a grant under Section 5307 or 5311 only if the applicant and any person that will receive benefits directly from the grant, are subject to the reporting and uniform systems.
The NTD reporting system evolved from the transit industry-initiated Project FARE (Uniform Financial Accounting and Reporting Elements). Both the private and public sectors have recognized the importance of timely and accurate data in assessing the continued progress of the nation's public transportation systems."

Title: Federal Transit Administration-National Transit Database (NTD)
Chunks: 0,1
"The NTD was established by Congress to be the Nation’s primary source for information and statistics on the transit systems of the United States. Recipients or beneficiaries of grants from the Federal Transit Administration (FTA) under the Urbanized Area Formula Program (§5307) or Other than Urbanized Area (Rural) Formula Program (§5311) are required by statute to submit data to the NTD. Over 660 transit providers in urbanized areas currently report to the NTD through the Internet-based reporting system. Each year, NTD performance data are used to apportion over $5 billion of FTA funds to transit agencies in urbanized areas (UZAs). Annual NTD reports are submitted to Congress summarizing transit service and safety data.
The legislative requirement for the NTD is found in Title 49 U.S.C. 5335(a):
SECTION 5335 National transit database
(a) NATIONAL TRANSIT DATABASE — To help meet the needs of individual public transportation systems, the United States Government, State and local governments, and the public for information on which to base public transportation service planning, the Secretary of Transportation shall maintain a reporting system, using uniform categories to accumulate public transportation financial and operating information and using a uniform system of accounts. The reporting and uniform systems shall contain appropriate information to help any level of government make a public sector investment decision. The Secretary may request and receive appropriate information from any source.
(b) REPORTING AND UNIFORM SYSTEMS — the Secretary may award a grant under Section 5307 or 5311 only if the applicant and any person that will receive benefits directly from the grant, are subject to the reporting and uniform systems.
The NTD reporting system evolved from the transit industry-initiated Project FARE (Uniform Financial Accounting and Reporting Elements). Both the private and public sectors have recognized the importance of timely and accurate data in assessing the continued progress of the nation's public transportation systems."

SL-5  UPWP Management
GOAL  
Conducting the day to day administrative, contract management, and financial planning activities that  
ensure that the MPO functions of the RPC staff and the TPC conform to adopted policy, as well as  
state and federal requirements.
OBJECTIVES  
•  Coordination of the TPC and all administrative and public requirements  
•  Preparation and management of contracts and agreements  
•  Fiscal responsibility and financial transparency  
•  Human resources which are necessary to ensure that staff have the wherewithal to conduct  
the everyday functions of the agency
PREVIOUS WORK  
•  The TPC has served as the MPO for the Slidell Urbanized Area under the provisions of  
SAFETEA-LU, MAP-21, and the FAST Act.  
•  The RPC hosts a meeting of the Regional Planning Commission and the Transportation Policy  
Committee on a monthly basis.  
•  RPC and TPC bylaws were updated in 2019  
•  Staff Policies and Procedures Manual, Staff Project Management Manual created in 2019

RPC staff will prepare and oversee contracts and intergovernmental agreements, ensuring that  
the necessary legal and contractual provisions, and guarantee these provisions are followed  
through the lifetime of the contract or agreement.

speakers, preparing budget and financial reports, making provisions for public participation, and  
preparing public notices announcing the meetings.

## [PDF page 98]
South Tangipahoa, which includes the cities of Hammond (pop.  20,768) and Ponchatoula  
(pop. 6,659), was designated as an urbanized area following the 2010 census. It is located  
northwest  of  New  Orleans,  west  of  St.  Tammany  Parish,  and  45  miles  east  of  Baton  
Rouge. Cities in the Urbanized Area include Hammond and Ponchatoula. In addition to  
being a major residential and employment center, Hammond is the home of Southeast  
Louisiana University.
Within  Tangipahoa Parish there are 321 miles of Federal Aid roadwa  ys, including two  
interstate  highways:  I  -12  and  I-55.  US  190  is  another  major  east-west  corridor  that  
connects major urban centers on the Northshore.
Fixed  route  public  transit  is  available  in  Hammond  and  Ponchatoula  with  demand  
response available parish-wide, provided by the parish government in partnership with  
the council on aging.
The Hammond Northshore Regional Airport, northeast of Hammond, is a 900 acre facility  
with two runways. A Canadian National rail line traverses the MPA from north to sout  h,  
also carrying Amtrak service.

SL-5  UPWP Management
GOAL  
Conducting the day to day administrative, contract management, and financial planning activities that  
ensure that the MPO functions of the RPC staff and the TPC conform to adopted policy, as well as  
state and federal requirements.
OBJECTIVES  
•  Coordination of the TPC and all administrative and public requirements  
•  Preparation and management of contracts and agreements  
•  Fiscal responsibility and financial transparency  
•  Human resources which are necessary to ensure that staff have the wherewithal to conduct  
the everyday functions of the agency
PREVIOUS WORK  
•  The TPC has served as the MPO for the Slidell Urbanized Area under the provisions of  
SAFETEA-LU, MAP-21, and the FAST Act.  
•  The RPC hosts a meeting of the Regional Planning Commission and the Transportation Policy  
Committee on a monthly basis.  
•  RPC and TPC bylaws were updated in 2019  
•  Staff Policies and Procedures Manual, Staff Project Management Manual created in 2019
TASKS
SL-5a: Contract Management and Intergovernmental Affairs  
RPC staff will prepare and oversee contracts and intergovernmental agreements, ensuring that  
the necessary legal and contractual provisions, and guarantee these provisions are followed  
through the lifetime of the contract or agreement.
Product(s)  
Major activities will be documented in the FY 2022 report.  
Timeline:  
Ongoing
SL-5b: Commission Coordination  
RPC staff will coordinate with the local elected officials and citizen representatives, including  
those that make up the Commission and the TPC, and conduct of the monthly commission  
meeting itself, including preparing agendas, minutes, meeting packets/material, scheduling guest  
speakers, preparing budget and financial reports, making provisions for public participation, and  
preparing public notices announcing the meetings.

South Tangipahoa, which includes the cities of Hammond (pop.  20,768) and Ponchatoula  
(pop. 6,659), was designated as an urbanized area following the 2010 census. It is located  
northwest  of  New  Orleans,  west  of  St.  Tammany  Parish,  and  45  miles  east  of  Baton  
Rouge. Cities in the Urbanized Area include Hammond and Ponchatoula. In addition to  
being a major residential and employment center, Hammond is the home of Southeast  
Louisiana University.
Within  Tangipahoa Parish there are 321 miles of Federal Aid roadwa  ys, including two  
interstate  highways:  I  -12  and  I-55.  US  190  is  another  major  east-west  corridor  that  
connects major urban centers on the Northshore.
Fixed  route  public  transit  is  available  in  Hammond  and  Ponchatoula  with  demand  
response available parish-wide, provided by the parish government in partnership with  
the council on aging.
The Hammond Northshore Regional Airport, northeast of Hammond, is a 900 acre facility  
with two runways. A Canadian National rail line traverses the MPA from north to sout  h,  
also carrying Amtrak service.

SL-5  UPWP Management
GOAL  
Conducting the day to day administrative, contract management, and financial planning activities that  
ensure that the MPO functions of the RPC staff and the TPC conform to adopted policy, as well as  
state and federal requirements.
OBJECTIVES  
•  Coordination of the TPC and all administrative and public requirements  
•  Preparation and management of contracts and agreements  
•  Fiscal responsibility and financial transparency  
•  Human resources which are necessary to ensure that staff have the wherewithal to conduct  
the everyday functions of the agency
PREVIOUS WORK  
•  The TPC has served as the MPO for the Slidell Urbanized Area under the provisions of  
SAFETEA-LU, MAP-21, and the FAST Act.  
•  The RPC hosts a meeting of the Regional Planning Commission and the Transportation Policy  
Committee on a monthly basis.  
•  RPC and TPC bylaws were updated in 2019  
•  Staff Policies and Procedures Manual, Staff Project Management Manual created in 2019
TASKS
SL-5a: Contract Management and Intergovernmental Affairs  
RPC staff will prepare and oversee contracts and intergovernmental agreements, ensuring that  
the necessary legal and contractual provisions, and guarantee these provisions are followed  
through the lifetime of the contract or agreement.
Product(s)  
Major activities will be documented in the FY 2022 report.  
Timeline:  
Ongoing

RPC staff will coordinate with the local elected officials and citizen representatives, including  
those that make up the Commission and the TPC, and conduct of the monthly commission  
meeting itself, including preparing agendas, minutes, meeting packets/material, scheduling guest  
speakers, preparing budget and financial reports, making provisions for public participation, and  
preparing public notices announcing the meetings.

## NTD Annual Data View - Service (by Agency)
Public Transit
This view provides transit agency-wide totals for service data for applicable agencies reporting to the National Transit Database in the 2022 - 2025 report years. This view is based off of the "2022 - 2025 NTD Annual Data - Service (by Mode and Time Period)" dataset, which displays the same data at a lower level of aggregation. This view displays the data at a higher level (by agency).
NTD Data Tables organize and summarize data from the 2022 - 2025 National Transit Database in a manner that is more useful for quick reference and summary analysis. The parent dataset is based on the 2022 - 2025 Service database files.
In years 2015-2021, you can find this data in the "Service" data table on NTD Program website, at https://transit.dot.gov/ntd/ntd-data.
In versions of the data tables from before 2014, you can find data on service in the file called "Transit Operating Statistics: Service Supplied and Consumed."
If you have any other questions about this table, please contact the NTD Help Desk at [NTDHelp@dot.gov](mailto:NTDHelp@dot.gov).
Read more

## Columns (43)
|  | Description |  |  |  
| --- | --- | --- | --- |  
| NTD ID | A five-digit identifying number for each agency used in the current NTD system. | _5_digit_ntd_id | Text |  
| Agency | The transit agency's name. | agency | Text |  
| Reporter Type | The type of NTD report that the agency completed this year. | max_reporter_type | Text |  
| Organization Type | Description of the agency's legal entity. | max_organization_type | Text |  
| City | The city in which the agency is headquartered. | max_city | Text |  
| State | The state in which the agency is headquartered. | max_state | Text |  
| Report Year | The year for which the data was reported. | report_year | Text |  
| Agency VOMS | The number of revenue vehicles operated across the whole agency to meet the annual maximum service requirement. This is the revenue vehicle count during the peak season of the year; on the week and day that maximum service is provided. Vehicles operated in maximum service (VOMS) exclude atypical days and one-time special events. Read more | max_agency_voms | Number |  
| UACE Code | UACE Code remains consistent across census years. | max_primary_uza_code | Text |  
| UZA Name | The name of the agency's Urbanized Area. | max_primary_uza_name | Text |  
| Primary UZA Area Sq Miles | The agency's Urbanized Area's size in square miles. | max_primary_uza_area_sq_miles | Number |  
| Primary UZA Population | The population of the urbanized area primarily served by the agency. | max_primary_uza_population | Number |  
| Service Area Sq Miles | The agency's service area's size in square miles. | max_service_area_sq_miles | Number |  
| Service Area Population | The population of the service area served by the agency. | max_service_area_population | Number |  
| Actual Vehicle/Passenger Car Miles | The miles that vehicles/passenger cars travel while in revenue service (actual vehicle revenue miles (VRM)) plus deadhead miles. Actual vehicle miles include: • Revenue service • Deadhead Actual vehicle miles exclude: • Miles for charter services • School bus service • Operator training • Vehicle maintenance testing Read more | sum_actual_vehicles_passenger_car_miles | Number |

The Federal Transit Administration sent this bulletin at 10/19/2026 02:25 PM EDT
* * * FTA has released the National Transit Database (NTD) Report Year 2025annual data products. Established in 1974, the NTD collects annual data from all FTA-funded transit agencies as well as voluntary reporters. This series of files includes data on ridership, safety, operating expenses, service levels, funding sources, and more from transit providers. The data release includes: * 2025 National Transit Summaries and Trends, which presents an overview of U.S. transit and highlights key transit metrics over the last decade. The document summarizes trends in an easy-to-read format with infographics, including maps of transit in the largest urbanized areas and a new exhibit about security trends. * All NTD Time Series and Database files available asinteractive datasets and visual summaries ondata.transportation.gov, the DOT's open data platform. * New row-level flags providing additional details: * Voluntary Reporter Flag in the Agency Information database file * ADA Accessibility Flag in the Facility Inventory database file There will be a NTD Data Product Updates webinar on Thursday, October 29, 2026 from 2:00pm to 3:30pm Eastern. ## NTD Annual Data View - Service (by Agency)
Public Transit
This view provides transit agency-wide totals for service data for applicable agencies reporting to the National Transit Database in the 2022 - 2025 report years. This view is based off of the "2022 - 2025 NTD Annual Data - Service (by Mode and Time Period)" dataset, which displays the same data at a lower level of aggregation. This view displays the data at a higher level (by agency).
NTD Data Tables organize and summarize data from the 2022 - 2025 National Transit Database in a manner that is more useful for quick reference and summary analysis. The parent dataset is based on the 2022 - 2025 Service database files.
In years 2015-2021, you can find this data in the "Service" data table on NTD Program website, at https://transit.dot.gov/ntd/ntd-data.
In versions of the data tables from before 2014, you can find data on service in the file called "Transit Operating Statistics: Service Supplied and Consumed."
If you have any other questions about this table, please contact the NTD Help Desk at [NTDHelp@dot.gov](mailto:NTDHelp@dot.gov).
